documents.title: Estuary floodgate operation
documents.content:
# Estuary floodgate operation

## Automatic closure
The East Reach gate closes automatically when the upstream gauge reaches 2.4 metres. The West Cut gate closes at 2.8 metres. Manual reopening requires clearance from the Tide Desk.

## Public warning
A steady amber beacon means automatic operation is enabled. A flashing violet beacon means maintenance isolation is active; it is not a flood warning.

documents.title: Floodgate control network
documents.content:
# Floodgate control network

The Selene controller operates the East Reach gate. The Oriole controller operates the West Cut gate. Both controllers report to the Tide Desk. The Tide Desk authorizes manual reopening after the upstream gauge has been checked.

## Loss of communications
If a controller loses communication for ninety seconds, its gate stays in its last commanded position. Communication loss does not authorize reopening.

documents.title: Floodgate maintenance rules
documents.content:
# Floodgate maintenance rules

## Before access
Notify the Tide Desk at least 24 hours before planned maintenance. Isolate hydraulic power and verify zero pressure before entering a gate enclosure.

## Recurring checks
Test both gate beacons every Monday. Calibrate upstream water-level gauges every twelve months. Record the gauge identifier and calibration date in the control register.

documents.title: Control-room reserve power
documents.content:
# Control-room reserve power

| Cabinet | Rated output | Reserve duration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Harbor | 120 watts | 6 hours |
| Ridge | 80 watts | 11 hours |

These durations were measured at the stated rated outputs. Colder conditions or heavier loads may reduce reserve duration. Reserve batteries power controllers and beacons, not the hydraulic gate motors.
